options: Compressing data so it occupies less disk space
Enabling parallel processing to fetch data
Converting text into numeric vectors for search
Encrypting data before it leaves a node
Sorting data before it is queried
questions.explanation: Data Vectorisation is about enabling parallel processing to fetch data, which is how MPP works at the back end.

questions.stem: In which processing mode does a computer or server traditionally work?
questions.explanation: Traditionally a machine works in SISD mode, Single Instruction Stream and Single Data Stream, fetching required data one item at a time.

questions.stem: When Data Vectorisation switches a system into MPP mode, which instruction model does it adopt?
questions.explanation: Data Vectorisation moves the system to SIMD, Single Instruction and Multiple Data, so one query pulls data from multiple nodes in parallel.

questions.stem: In Data Vectorisation, what happens when one query is executed and the data resides in multiple data nodes?
options: Data from all nodes is pulled in parallel
Each node is queried one after another
Only the first node is read
The query is rejected until the data is consolidated
The data is first copied to a single node
questions.explanation: Under SIMD or MPP mode, a single query pulls data from all nodes in parallel, making computation much faster than sequential SISD.

questions.stem: Since which developments has Data Vectorisation become a key component of data solutions?
questions.explanation: Data Vectorisation became prominent with Big Data: since Hadoop, NoSQL databases and Cloud surfaced, most databases are vectorisation or MPP enabled.

questions.stem: Which kinds of datasets created the need for Data Vectorisation in the Big Data era?
options: Social media, CCTV and audio datasets
questions.explanation: Organisations began storing and utilising social media, CCTV and audio datasets, which are far too large to process sequentially.

questions.stem: Why was non-vectorised processing unsuitable for huge datasets?
options: Because it cannot handle structured data
Because it requires a cloud subscription
Because it is incompatible with SQL
Because processing gigabytes and terabytes sequentially would take days
Because it produces less accurate results
questions.explanation: Processing gigabytes and terabytes in sequential SISD mode would take days, so massively parallel SIMD processing was chosen instead.

questions.stem: How much faster does Data Vectorisation make computation compared with SISD, according to *I Am Datapedia!*?
questions.explanation: Massively parallel processing makes computation hundreds of times faster than SISD or non-vectorised processing.

questions.stem: Which two of the four instruction models does the Data Vectorisation discussion focus on?
questions.explanation: The vectorisation discussion refers only to SISD, the traditional sequential mode, and SIMD, the parallel mode adopted under MPP.

questions.stem: Which statement about Data Vectorisation is NOT correct?
options: It was in use before Big Data but was not famous
It explains how MPP works at the back end
Most databases are now vectorisation or MPP enabled
It became common since the inception of Big Data or Hadoop
It can only be used with structured relational data
questions.explanation: Data Vectorisation is precisely what makes processing of huge social media, CCTV and audio datasets feasible; it is not limited to structured relational data.
